CanonAdditions: Caelen awakened in a pit formed from local earth.
Caelen's new body is physically distinct from his previous Marine body, featuring larger, broad-palmed hands and tanned, rough skin.
The gravity on Caelen's new world is heavier than Earth's, or his body is unaccustomed to its own weight.
Caelen's new world has a pale, washed-out yellow sky and a dim, hazy sun.
Caelen does not speak or understand the local language of his new world.
Caelen was captured by three men who assessed his physical condition.
Caelen was struck across the ribs by the man with the staff during his capture.
Caelen was fitted with a metal collar that locked around his neck.
Caelen was placed in a wooden cart and transported away from the capture site.
Caelen is currently enslaved and being treated as an asset or object of trade.
CanonChangesOverTime: Caelen was dead and suspended in the void; Caelen is now alive and physically present in a new world.
Caelen was free of physical constraints; Caelen is now bound with a metal collar and has his arms bound behind his back.
Caelen was in a formless void; Caelen is now in a physical environment with gravity, air, and sensory input.
WorldStateUpdates: The current world has a pale yellow sky and a dim sun.
The current world features a society with slavery, where individuals are assessed, collared, and transported in carts.
The current world has a language that is alien to Caelen, characterized by harsh consonants and rolling vowels.
The current world has a physical environment with wet earth, rot, and metallic smells in the resurrection pit.

Updates: Caelen exists and is an established character.
Caelen is alive and physically present in a new world.
Caelen is in a new body that is physically distinct from his previous one, with larger hands and tanned skin.
Caelen is currently enslaved, wearing a locked metal collar, and has his arms bound behind his back.
Caelen has sustained a fresh injury to his ribs from being struck by a staff.
Caelen does not understand the local language.
Caelen is currently being transported in a wooden cart.
The Man in the Tunic exists and is an established character.
The Man in the Tunic is a male with dark, weathered skin and narrow, sharp eyes.
The Man in the Tunic wears a coarse brown tunic and a leather belt with a short, curved blade.
The Man in the Tunic participated in Caelen's capture and assessment.
The Staff-Bearer exists and is an established character.
The Staff-Bearer is one of the three men who captured Caelen.
The Staff-Bearer holds a short staff and struck Caelen across the ribs.
The Staff-Bearer read from a leather-bound book during the assessment.
The Blue-Clothed Man exists and is an established character.
The Blue-Clothed Man is a male wearing a deep blue silk tunic and a crown of twisted metal.
The Blue-Clothed Man holds a ledger and a quill.
The Blue-Clothed Man assessed Caelen and authorized his transport as a slave.

NarrativeStateUpdates: The narrative has moved from Caelen's time in the void to his resurrection and immediate enslavement.
Caelen has been captured, assessed, collared, and placed in a cart for transport.
Caelen has acknowledged his status as a slave and resolved to learn the local language and rules to find a way out.
UnresolvedInformation: The specific location or name of the world Caelen has arrived in is not stated.
The identity or name of the owner or master to whom Caelen is being sold is not established.
The specific meaning of the numbers '1' and '1' in the System interface remains unexplained to Caelen.
ExtractionWarnings: The text states 'The gravity on this world was heavier than Earth’s, or perhaps his body was simply unaccustomed to the weight of its own flesh.' It is ambiguous whether the gravity is objectively heavier or if it is a subjective perception due to the new body's condition.
